decision: account creation: first-run setup screen, later accounts via CLI; no signup, no roles
why: user picked the recommended option

decision: isolation: conversations, artifacts, attachments, search, screenshots, workspaces and trusted domains per user; org skills, model, MCP shared
why: org skills are org-wide by name; trusted domains govern only the owner's artifact pages

decision: capacity stays global; capacity views and errors list only the caller's own holders
why: smallest change that leaks no other user's conversations

decision: stay loopback-only; no TLS or LAN exposure in this PR
why: passwords and cookies over plain http to the LAN deserve their own change

decision: scrypt hashes, opaque session token in HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie stored hashed, 30-day expiry, auth always on, first account adopts unowned data
why: defaults stated in round 1 (Q5-Q7) that the user did not override

decision: owner lives in ConversationMeta.owner, written in the creating commit
why: atomic with creation and list already reads MetaDoc; a side table could orphan a conversation on a crash between writes

decision: one ownership guard in the Authentication middleware keyed on the URL (/api/conversations/:id and ?conversation=), reused by the shell socket
why: every conversation-addressed route passes one choke point, so a new route cannot forget the check

decision: staged upload ids stay capabilities, no owner column
why: they are 128-bit random and only reach the uploader; a sent upload belongs to its conversation, which the guard covers

decision: the guard reads any URL segment after 'conversations' and any conversation= value that Number() can parse, after decoding
why: params like +1, %31 or 1.0 can decode to conversation 1, so a digits-only regex would let a crafted URL past the check

decision: replaced Artifacts.listAll with listIn(conversationIds) and deleted listAll
why: an unscoped listing is exactly the leak this feature closes; no caller should be able to reach it

decision: search filters by owned conversation ids inside the FTS SQL (json_each), not after
why: filtering after the 200-row cap would let other users' hits starve a user's results

decision: CapacityExhausted and /api/capacity keep shared limits but list only the caller's holders and waiters
why: grilling Q3; holders are other people's conversation ids otherwise

decision: adoption of pre-account data runs at setup and again on every start for the oldest account
why: idempotent, so a crash between creating the first account and adopting finishes on the next boot

decision: pnpm check green: 589 server tests, 402 web tests, lint, format, typecheck
why: gate before browser and docker checks

decision: broke the ownership check on purpose (if false) and reran the isolation matrix
why: a matrix that passes with the guard disabled proves nothing
result: fails with guard off, passes with it on

decision: seeded a pre-account database with main's own server (one conversation, one trusted domain), then ran the branch on it
why: adoption and the trusted_domains rebuild are only proven against data the old code wrote

decision: browser run over Docker sandboxes: setup, adoption, shell socket, wrong password, CLI-added second user, isolation of lists/search/artifacts/attachments/capacity/shell
why: the real surface, not the faux harness

decision: artifact page image failed with 401 inside the sandboxed iframe
why: opaque-origin iframe requests are cross-site, so SameSite=Lax cookies are never sent

decision: moved attachment thumbnail and PDF page images to an attachmentImages group outside Authentication; the 128-bit attachment id plus its own conversation is the capability
why: SameSite=None needs Secure (browser-dependent on http) and drops CSRF protection; per-render signed grants would mean rewriting agent HTML
result: artifact image loads; original and view still 401

decision: iris captures of the signed-out screens in light, dark and iphone
why: the user asked for iris screenshots; iris has no cookie support so signed-in screens came from Playwright

decision: cross-model review (sonnet) found the URL guard bypassed by /api/Conversations/2, /api/%63onversations/2 and /api/conversations//2, which Effect's router still matches
why: the guard parsed the raw URL; the premise that it could predict the router's decoding was wrong

decision: guard now reads the matched route: the endpoint's path template plus HttpRouter.params and ParsedSearchParams; the shell route passes its template
why: use the router's own decoding instead of re-deriving it, so no spelling can differ

decision: isolation test sends every scoped route in the review's spellings as bob and checks alice reaches her history through them; the old raw-URL reader swapped back fails it
why: a variant test that passes because the router never served the spelling would prove nothing
result: fails on old guard, passes on new

decision: replayed the review's bypass URLs on the real server: alice 200, bob 404 for all; stop/pause via variants 404
why: re-check the real artifact after the fix

decision: sign-in throttle charges the attempt before verifying, and bounds the per-name map
why: review: parallel guesses all read count 0 and never reached the block
evidence: src/auth/auth.ts login; auth.test.ts burst test (12 parallel: old code 12 through, new 5)

decision: loopbackOnly pins browser Origin and X-Forwarded-Host to WEB_PORT and SERVER_PORT
why: review: SameSite ignores ports, so a page on any other local port could send the cookie and open the shell socket
evidence: src/server/loopback.ts pagePorts; origin 5173 → 403, 3101 → 200 on the real server

decision: second failure in the 19/21 run was the image upload: a 2x2 PNG was refused (400); a 64x64 one uploads
why: supersedes the 19/21 row, which traced only one failure

decision: left open: setup goes to whoever reaches the console first; adoption runs at every boot for the oldest account
why: both follow from the grilling answers; documented in AGENTS.md Accounts and the PR
